messages:
ashley: Heads-up — customer asked for a short playbook and guarantees around audit events: coverage, per-tenant proofs, and how we handle spikes. Also they want assurances about KMS key usage and rotation. Can we sketch a runbook and performance controls?

devon: +1. do we mean cryptographic proofs (signed events) or just structured audit exports?

ashley: Both. They want signed event batches so a tenant can verify integrity. Also need to document which events are considered PII and encrypted with tenant KMS.

marco: For ingestion scale, we should avoid per-event KMS calls. Use envelope encryption: tenant DEK (data encryption key) encrypted with tenant KEK (KMS). We rotate KEKs via KMS and rotate DEKs periodically in-worker. That keeps KMS ops to DEK wraps/unwrapps, not per-event.

samir: +1 on envelope. For signed proofs we can produce a per-tenant batch signature: worker collects N events or time window, canonicalizes JSON, signs with an ephemeral signing key tied to the tenant (rotated daily). We store signature metadata alongside the batch in audit-store.

ashley: Can we show a tiny example of canonicalization + signing format? Need something to include in the customer-facing doc.

marco: Sure — pseudo: 
```
// example canonical event array
[ {"ts":"2026-11-02T12:00:00Z","actor":"svc-account","action":"model.invoke","resource":"/v1/generate","id":"evt_123"}, ... ]
// canonical string: JSON stringify with keys sorted, no whitespace
\n// signature metadata
{"tenant":"t-789","batch_id":"b-20261102-0001","signed_by":"signer-rot-20261102","signature":"MEUCIQ..."}
```

samir: Important: keep canonicalization deterministic across language bindings. We should publish a tiny reference lib in python/node.

devon: On the throughput/cost side: batching reduces KMS and signing ops but increases reorder/latency. For high QPS tenants we should use adaptive batch thresholds: either size-based (msgs) or time-based (ms). Recommend defaults: 200 events or 1s, with per-tenant overrides.

ashley: What about indexing/storage costs? Customers asked whether signed batches will increase ES/longterm storage.

marco: Signed batches add minimal payload: signature ~280 bytes + metadata per batch. We can keep per-event documents the same (no duplication) and store signature as a separate 'batch' record. For retention: we can TTL raw events but keep signatures/manifest for verifiability until retention expires. That reduces per-event index cost.

samir: Also consider compressing batch payloads before long-term archive (s3 gz). For queries we index only necessary fields; raw full events can go to cold storage. That reduces index shard count and cost.

devon: Backpressure: current ingest pipeline already has a per-tenant token-bucket and priority queue. For signed batches we need a slight change: signing workers must be part of the critical path. If signing falls behind, we should still accept events and mark batch as 'unsigned-pending' with a durable queue, not drop. But we should set quotas and circuit-breakers so a noisy tenant doesn't fill queue.

ashley: Good point. Concrete playbook steps?

marco: Draft playbook: 
1) Detection: high event rate triggers tenant-rate >= X and queue depth > Y -> alert oncall.
2) Mitigation: auto-throttle new writes for that tenant (token bucket drop or 429/soft-queue).
3) Graceful degrade: accept events to durable cold queue for later signing/processing, but mark them as 'delayed-sign'. Return 202 + header indicating delay ETA.
4) Recovery: spawn ramped signing workers, apply backfill windows. Notify customer via audit-subscription webhook when delayed batches are signed.
5) Postmortem: collect metrics (signing-lag, KMS ops/sec, storage delta) and cost impact.

samir: For KMS limits, we must track KMS ops per-tenant and set soft-limits. Some clouds limit Encrypt/Decrypt calls. Envelope approach keeps ops low (wrap/unwrap per rollover + on-demand), but signing keys might be stored in KMS-managed HSM or in a separate signing service using HSM-backed keys. Need architecture note.

devon: For immediate implementation: 1) build per-tenant batcher + signing worker, 2) enqueue signed-batch record and per-event pointer, 3) expose /audit/verify endpoint where tenants can ask for batch manifest and signature.

ashley: Any security vulnerabilities or vuln triage implications? We just had CVE-2026-XXXXX in our json-parser lib — does canonicalization expose us?

marco: We should pin canonicalization lib to a patched version and add CI verify step. Also ensure canonicalize() rejects unknown types and normalizes unicode. Document this in the playbook as a required step for customer proofs (otherwise signature mismatch).

samir: Ops checklist for oncall: how to tell customers about delayed signatures, commands to flush queues, and a script to re-sign archived batches if signer rotated. I'll draft sample kubectl/job steps.

ashley: Great. Can someone write the short customer-facing FAQ: what signed events mean, expected latency, how to verify, and cost implications? Keep it simple.

devon: I'll draft it. Also propose conservative defaults for free tier tenants (no signing) and opt-in for paid tiers due to cost.

sec-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1981 — audit-signing-playbook requested by @ashley, assigned to devon/marco/samir.

ashley: Thanks — more later. I'll collect these into a 1-page playbook and a small reference lib issue.
